rationale: Evidence confirms that PLP1 null syndrome manifests with a mild multifocal demyelinating peripheral neuropathy, which distinguishes it from typical SPAX8 presentations where peripheral nerve involvement is primarily categorized as axonal. However, literature examining Charcot-Marie-Tooth and related neuropathies also links NKX6-2 to mixed demyelinating and axonal lesions with reduced nerve conduction velocities, and PLP1 duplications/missense variants do not uniformly present with frank demyelinating neuropathy, making the distinction on nerve conduction studies alone less absolute than hypothesized.

evidence.text: PLP1 null variants are associated with mild demyelinating neuropathy, serving as a differential diagnostic criterion from NKX6-2-related hypomyelinating disorders.

conflicts: Demyelinating peripheral neuropathy in PLP1-related disorders is predominantly restricted to the PLP1 null syndrome and is typically mild and multifocal rather than a generalized frank demyelinating sensorimotor polyneuropathy across all PLP1 genotypes.

NKX6-2 has been indexed in neuropathy cohorts displaying intermediate or demyelinating features with reduced nerve conduction velocities, contradicting the assertion that peripheral conduction slowing/demyelinating patterns never occur in SPAX8.

new_directions.question_text: Does electrophysiological evaluation of motor and sensory nerves in confirmed SPAX8 cohorts show uniform preservation of conduction velocities or subclinical intermediate slowing?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying whether NKX6-2 variants cause true secondary paranodopathies or mixed conduction slowing in peripheral nerves would determine whether electrophysiology can reliably rule out SPAX8.

new_directions.question_text: What proportion of classic Pelizaeus-Merzbacher disease (PLP1 duplications) versus PMLD1 (GJC2) patients demonstrate demyelinating peripheral nerve conduction profiles compared to PLP1 null syndrome?
new_directions.rationale: If demyelinating neuropathy is absent in classic PMD and PMLD1, using demyelinating neuropathy as a general discriminator against SPAX8 will produce high false-negative rates.
